item.title: Episode 43 – Wrath of the Khans I
item.description:
About this episode

The opening chapter introduces the Mongol world and the extraordinary eruption of steppe nomads into the great societies of Eurasia. It sets up the central question of the series: how did a relatively small population create an empire of such enormous scale and violence?

Key ideas

  • The Eurasian steppe and its societies
  • The rise of the Mongols
  • Genghis Khan and the foundations of the empire
  • Mobility, horses and steppe warfare
  • The human cost of Mongol expansion

Series context: This is the starting point for the conquest story that continues through China, the Islamic world and Europe.

item.title: Episode 44 – Wrath of the Khans II
item.description:
About this episode

Genghis Khan's conquests move into major settled civilizations. The episode follows the Mongol campaigns against Northern China and the Eastern Islamic world and examines the strategic qualities behind the Mongols' astonishing military success.

Key ideas

  • Genghis Khan as military strategist
  • Northern China and the Islamic world
  • Siege warfare and adaptation
  • Fear, reputation and psychological warfare
  • The enormous human cost of conquest
item.itunes:title: Episode 44 – Wrath of the Khans II
item.itunes:author: Dan Carlin
item.itunes:summary: Genghis Khan's campaigns against Northern China and the Eastern Islamic world, and the strategy behind Mongol expansion.

item.title: Episode 45 – Wrath of the Khans III
item.description:
About this episode

The Mongol expansion continues across an enormous geographic area. The episode follows the consequences of Mongol warfare as the empire pushes farther into Europe and China and explores whether any power can stop the momentum.

Key ideas

  • Continued Mongol expansion
  • Europe and China under pressure
  • Mongol military organization and mobility
  • Retaliation and terror as instruments of war
  • The limits of resistance to the Mongol armies
item.itunes:title: Episode 45 – Wrath of the Khans III
item.itunes:author: Dan Carlin
item.itunes:summary: The Mongol conquests expand toward Europe and China, testing whether any power can halt their momentum.

item.title: Episode 46 – Wrath of the Khans IV
item.description:
About this episode

Genghis Khan dies, but the Mongol war machine does not slow down. Instead, the empire's expansion accelerates, with Europe increasingly drawn into the story.

Key ideas

  • The death of Genghis Khan
  • Succession and imperial continuity
  • The Mongol advance toward Europe
  • European encounters with Mongol warfare
  • Why the empire continued expanding after its founder
item.itunes:title: Episode 46 – Wrath of the Khans IV
item.itunes:author: Dan Carlin
item.itunes:summary: After Genghis Khan's death, Mongol expansion accelerates and Europe becomes a major target.

item.title: Episode 47 – Wrath of the Khans V
item.description:
About this episode

The final main chapter turns to succession and the grandchildren of Genghis Khan. The empire faces internal competition over inheritance while Mongol rulers continue to combine conquest with administration and governance.

Key ideas

  • Succession after the great conquests
  • The grandchildren of Genghis Khan
  • Imperial fragmentation and competing claims
  • Mongol administration and governance
  • The long-term fate of the Mongol Empire
item.itunes:title: Episode 47 – Wrath of the Khans V
item.itunes:author: Dan Carlin
item.itunes:summary: Succession, competing imperial claims and the changing Mongol Empire after Genghis Khan.

item.title: Episode 47 EXTRA – Wrath of the Khans
item.description:
About this episode

A Director's Cut-style companion to Episode 47. It contains additional military-history discussion, cutting-room-floor material, Dan's reflections on the challenges of making the episode, and thoughts on why he constructed Wrath of the Khans as he did.

Best listened to

After Episode 47, as a companion and behind-the-scenes addendum to the series.
